title: Permuting the columns multiplies the determinant by the sign
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $m\ge0$ an integer, $M=(M_{it})$ an $m\times m$ matrix with entries in $R$ [def-weil-matrix] and $\tau$ a permutation of $\{1,\dots,m\}$ with sign $\operatorname{sgn}(\tau)\in\{\pm1\}$. Let $M'$ be the $m\times m$ matrix with $M'_{ik}=M_{i,\tau(k)}$ (column $k$ of $M'$ is column $\tau(k)$ of $M$). Then $\det M'=\operatorname{sgn}(\tau)\det M$ [def-weil-pbc-matrix-determinant].

source.place: Algebra, Section Tag 00AR (section-rings-basic), list item Tag 0F0K (item-cauchy-binet, line 282), stated there without proof; the behaviour of the determinant under a permutation of the columns is a basic property used in the proof of the item
